issues.legal_issue: A price agreed between interested parties does not control the statutory determination of compensation for acquired land.
material_facts: The railway had agreed to pay a stated price per bigha before acquisition proceedings began, but the purchase was not completed.
The company relied on the agreed price in challenging the compensation award.
The Court did not decide whether the agreement was a concluded contract.
issues.conclusion: The agreement, even if binding between the parties, did not prevent the Collector or the court on reference from independently determining the land’s market value.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 11 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, the Collector and the court on reference perform a statutory duty and must exercise their own judgment on the correct basis of valuation; an agreement between interested parties cannot control that judgment. The Court relied on Fort Press Company Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay and Moulvi Samiullah v. Collector of Aligarh.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerned compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.parties_agreed_on_price: The interested parties had agreed on a price for the land.

issues.definition: When a compensation proceeding concerns acquired land and the interested parties agreed on a price, the valuation authority must independently determine market value.

issues.legal_issue: A market-value finding cannot stand where it rests on inadequately examined sale evidence and relevant comparable-sale evidence is rejected without sufficient inquiry.
material_facts: The lower courts relied principally on an official statement of six sales compiled from office and registration records.
The official who prepared the statement had not visited the sale sites and could not describe the circumstances of the transactions or establish that the plots were comparable.
The prices in the listed sales varied substantially, and the reasons for the disparity were not explained.
The company produced two sale deeds, which the High Court rejected without adequately examining their relevance or, in one instance, asking the purchaser why the price had been paid.
The High Court treated the official sale statement as conclusive without addressing its limitations or other important evidence.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s market-value determination could not stand, and the matter required reconsideration.
issues.legal_principle: Market value must be determined on an adequate assessment of relevant evidence. Sale transactions must be shown to be comparable, and the evidence relied on must be scrutinized for its circumstances and limitations; a finding cannot be treated as conclusive while material infirmities and relevant evidence remain unexamined.

predicates.land_acquisition_market_value_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal concerning the market value of acquired land.
predicates.valuation_based_on_unverified_sales: The valuation finding relied on sales whose circumstances or characteristics had not been adequately verified.
predicates.comparability_not_established: The evidence did not establish that the sale plots were comparable to the acquired land.
predicates.relevant_sale_evidence_rejected_without_: Relevant sale evidence was rejected without adequate examination of its circumstances.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning acquired land rests on inadequately verified sales and either comparability is not established or relevant sale evidence is rejected without inquiry, the market-value finding requires reconsideration.

issues.legal_issue: Where market value is to be reconsidered and rental information is incomplete, the determination may be remitted for valuation by capitalizing rental value on affidavit evidence.
material_facts: The High Court had found no objection to determining market value by capitalizing rental value over a period of twenty years.
Evidence indicated that the railway had taken the land on lease at an annual rent, but the other terms of the lease were unknown and it was unclear whether the lease was written.
The case was old, and the Court considered a remand for new and additional material to the District Judge undesirable.
The Court remitted the matter to the High Court to determine market value by the rental-capitalization method on affidavits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was to determine market value by capitalizing rental value on the basis of affidavit evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the rental-capitalization method as an available means of determining market value in this case and directed the High Court to assess the necessary material on affidavits, given the uncertainty about the lease terms and the age of the case.

predicates.land_acquisition_market_value_remand: The proceeding required a renewed determination of the market value of acquired land.
predicates.rental_arrangement_evidence_incomplete: Evidence of a rental arrangement existed, but its terms were not fully known.

issues.definition: When a renewed determination of acquired land’s market value is needed and rental-arrangement evidence is incomplete, market value is determined by rental capitalization on affidavits.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal may be considered as one by special leave despite an unreasoned certificate where the questions involved warrant consideration.
material_facts: The High Court granted a certificate to appeal that disclosed no reasons.
The respondents objected that the certificate should be cancelled.
The Court considered the questions raised in the appeal to warrant consideration and heard it as one by special leave.
issues.conclusion: The Court treated the appeal as one by special leave and considered it despite the certificate’s lack of reasons.
issues.legal_principle: Although the certificate was defective because it gave no reasons, the Court could hear the matter as an appeal by special leave when the questions involved warranted consideration.

predicates.appeal_presented_under_high_court_certif: The proceeding was presented as an appeal under a certificate granted by a High Court.
predicates.certificate_gives_no_reasons: The certificate contained no reasons for granting it.
predicates.questions_warrant_consideration: The questions raised in the appeal warranted consideration by the Court.

issues.definition: When an appeal is presented under an unreasoned High Court certificate and its questions warrant consideration, it is heard as an appeal by special leave.
